summary: Return the length (in edges) of the longest path between any two nodes in a binary tree.
mainInsight: The longest path through a node uses its deepest left and deepest right descent: left height + right height. Compute heights bottom-up, update a global best at every node, and return the usual height to the parent.

approaches.name: Height at every node
approaches.summary: For each node compute left and right heights separately.

approaches.name: One-pass postorder
approaches.summary: dfs returns height; best = max(best, left + right).

personalSolution.approach: One-pass postorder with a nonlocal best

cards.answer: Return the height up; record left + right in a global at each node
cards.explanation: The parent needs the height (one branch), while the best path may bend at any node using both branches.

promptVariants: Why is the diameter not necessarily through the root?
Why do you return a different value than you record?
cards.answer: The longest path can bend at any node: the best path whose highest node is v has length left_height(v) + right_height(v). So we record that at every node. But a path extending upward from v can only use one of v's branches, so the function returns the single-branch height 1 + max(left, right) for the parent.
keyPoints: Path bends at its highest node
cards.explanation: The same 'record vs return' split solves Maximum Path Sum.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Recursion stack space: ___
Why does `best = max(best, maxLeft + maxRight)` count edges and not nodes, and what does the function return for a leaf?
cards.code:
def dfs(root):
    nonlocal best
    if not root:
        return 0
    maxLeft = dfs(root.left)
    maxRight = dfs(root.right)
    best = max(best, maxLeft + maxRight)
    return max(maxLeft, maxRight) + 1
cards.answer: dfs returns heights counted in nodes. A branch of height h hanging below v contributes exactly h edges to a path through v (one edge to the child plus the edges inside), so the path bending at v has leftHeight + rightHeight edges. A leaf returns 1; an empty tree 0 so that a node with one child gets maxRight = 0.
keyPoints: left + right = edges on the bent path
